ledger.x: 1035: Ramiro I receives Aragon on his father's death.
1043: Ramiro annexes Sobrarbe and Ribagorza.
1043 at the latest: Sangüesa passes to Ramiro.
1064 (August): a Christian army takes Barbastro.
17 April 1065: the Muslims retake Barbastro.
1076: Sancho Ramírez becomes King of Pamplona.
1083: Graus is taken.
1089: Monzón is conquered.
1096 (end of November): Peter I takes Huesca.
1096: the capital moves from Jaca to Huesca.
1100: the Aragonese take Barbastro and the Cinca.
1105: Alfonso I takes Ejea and Tauste.
1107: Alfonso I takes La Litera.
18 December 1118: Alfonso I takes Zaragoza.
1119: Alfonso I retakes towns and populates Soria.
ledger.cp: holders of the Soria towns (the page names none)

ledger.x: 25 February 1119: Alfonso I takes Tudela.
1120: Calatayud falls and Daroca with it.
The Castilian possessions of Alfonso I in Cliopatria's 1126 shape.
1127: Alfonso I loses Castile.
1134: Navarre separates from Aragon.
13 November 1137: Ramiro II abdicates; Ramon Berenguer IV rules Aragon.
1146: García Ramírez of Navarre occupies Tauste.
1146: Alfonso VII mediates.
1162: the Kingdom of Aragon enters the Crown of Aragon.

wars.name: Ramiro I's war with García Sánchez III of Navarre
wars.outcome: Ramiro was defeated at Tafalla but gained territory, including Sangüesa.

wars.name: Battle of Graus
wars.outcome: Ramiro I died on 8 May 1063 at Graus 'while trying to take the city'; Graus was conquered by his son in 1083.

wars.name: Crusade of Barbastro
wars.outcome: A Christian army, 'the largest component was Aquitainian', took Barbastro after a forty-day siege in August 1064 and Armengol III of Urgel was 'entrusted with the government of the city'; the Muslims retook it on 17 April 1065.

wars.name: Siege of Huesca and Battle of Alcoraz
wars.outcome: Sancho Ramírez began the siege in 1094 and died before the city; Peter I beat the relief army of Al-Musta'in II of Zaragoza at Alcoraz on 15 November 1096 and Huesca surrendered less than two weeks later.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of the Cinca
wars.outcome: Barbastro, Sariñena, Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca were captured ('1100-1101'; 'Barbastro fell in 1100', Peter I page).

wars.name: Alfonso I's first campaigns against Zaragoza
wars.outcome: Ejea and Tauste conquered in 1105; Ahmad II al-Musta'in of Zaragoza defeated at Valtierra in 1106; Tamarite de Litera and San Esteban de Litera taken in 1107.

wars.name: Conquest of Zaragoza and the Ebro valley
wars.outcome: Zaragoza fell on 18 December 1118; Calatayud and Daroca in 1120 after the Battle of Cutanda (1120), where Alfonso defeated a Muslim army 'intent on reconquering his new capital'.

wars.name: Alfonso I's Castilian war
wars.outcome: Alfonso VII took all of Alfonso I's Castilian possessions in 1127; the Peace of Támara (1128) set the boundary between the realms.

wars.name: Battle of Fraga
wars.outcome: Alfonso's last campaigns, against Mequinenza (1133) and Fraga (1134), ended in an unsuccessful battle; he died in September 1134.

wars.name: Navarrese-Aragonese incident at Tauste
wars.outcome: García Ramírez 'occupied Tauste, which belonged to Aragon'; 'Alfonso VII intervened to mediate a peace between the two kingdoms'.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on any page opened for the Muslim frontier or for Navarre; counties and conquests are named by town.
The Peace of Támara (1128) 'set the boundary between the two realms', so the Castilian frontier is the one sharp line; the Navarrese frontier after 1134 and the Muslim frontier stay soft.
